newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Mch 24.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Mch 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia is back in the third cricket Test against South Africa after Glenn McGrath claimed three wickets in his first 10 overs, as South Africa crashed to 7-298 at lunch on the first day, a first innings lead of 71. McGrath had figures of 5-67 at the break. Page 25.

Queensland is favourite to win cricket's Sheffield Shield final against Western Australia in Perth after Trevor Barsby, in his final Shield game, scored 111 on the third day. At stumps Queensland were 6-259 in their second innings, with an overall lead of414 with six sessions remaining. Page 27.

The Australian Cycling Federation has extended the qualifying deadline for the world titles in Perth later this year. This will allow currently injured riders, including Kathy Watt, to make a further bid for selection. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor will remain in South Africa for the seven one-day matches, despite speculation he would be rested. Batsmen Matthew Hayden, Matthew Elliot and Justin Langer will return home to be replaced by new players Michael Di Veuto, Stuart Law and Brendon Julian. Page 29.

Soccer Australia has reduced the national soccer league from 14 to 12 clubs, with the Collingwood Warriors, Canberra Cosmos and the Gippsland Falcons being dropped. Carlton is the only new side, with sacked clubs able to earn a reprieve if they can prove trong financial support. Page 28.

Super League chief executive John Ribot has defended the new competition after the Australian Rugby League scored a resounding victory on spectator numbers over the weekend. Six ARL matches drew 74,527 fans, with the four Super League matches pulling only36,353 fans. The final round-four Super League game between Canberra and Brisbane will be played tonight. Page 27.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League will pay compensation to St Kilda and Hawthorn in an attempt to bring them to the new Docklands Stadium. The clubs could take the AFL to court if they do not receive lucrative deals of over $1 million each to endorse the newmove. Page Sport 3.

Carlton has defeated Geelong by 57 points in the pre-season Ansett Cup grand final. The Blues played strongly in winning the $105,000 competition, and exposed Geelong's frailties under pressure. Page Sport 6.

Honda riders John Kocinski and Aaron Slight have won the Superbike opening round at Phillip Island ahead of two times world champion Carl Fogarty and Simon Crafar. Only eighteen of the starting field of 30 finished the race due to the inclement weather. Page Sport 10.
THE HERALD SUN

Collingwood will hold talks this week with a syndicate group which is willing to spend $200 million on Waverley Park. The Group would like the Magpies to play their home games at the park, which would be developed into the world's first sporting theme park.Page 80.

Collingwood has sacked Trent Hotton after he arrived in an unacceptable condition to a team meeting. He had received previous warnings about his off-field behaviour, including a New Year's Eve incident after which he was fined A$600. Page 78.

West Australian Kim Felton has defeated Queensland's Derrin Morgan in the final of the Australian men's amateur golf championship at Lake Karrinyup. Felton will now be included in the national squad for two overseas tournaments later this year. Page 77.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Cronulla and Canterbury were both defeated yesterday in surprise Super League results. Cronulla were thrashed 38-10 by Penrith, and Canterbury were defeated 34-6 by the Perth Reds. Penrith remain undefeated in the competition after four rounds. Page 35.

Sydney City and Manly share the lead in the Australian Rugby League competition after both had wins in round three games. Souths scored a surprise 17-8 victory over Wests, with Newcastle scoring the biggest win of the round, 44-0 over South Queensland. Page 36.

The ACT Brumbies have scored a strong win against Canterbury 49-29 in the Super 12 rugby union series. The Brumbies share fourth place, with the Gauteng Lions (formerly known as Transvaal) in the lead after four unbeaten matches. Page 44.
